_comment: Process files in `order` with one shared dedupe set, then the OpenCode database, then the Antigravity databases in `antigravity.order` (same dedupe set). Paths are relative to this folder. `mtimes` (Unix ms) give the modification times that produce both orders; apply them to a copy of this folder before computing daily history. `traces` (Gemini, omp) give the phase after feeding a file up to and including physical line `afterLine` (after the files before it in `order`). omp: the folder `omp` plays ~/.omp, so its automatic roots are omp/agent/sessions and omp/profiles/*/agent/sessions; `omp.discover` lists what discovery finds there. Antigravity: the folder `antigravity` plays ~/.gemini (stores antigravity-cli, antigravity, antigravity-ide); each database is one agent whose id is its path; `{"unsupported": true}` marks a database that contributes no agent; reading must not create any file (no -wal or -shm). WorkBuddy: the folder `workbuddy` plays the home folder (data folders .workbuddy and .workbuddy-ai); `workbuddy.discover` lists what discovery finds in both projects folders; its `traces` work like the omp ones. Pi: the folder `pi` plays ~/.pi with this folder as home (pi/agent/settings.json names the custom session folder ~/pi/custom-sessions); `pi.discover` lists what discovery finds in both roots; its `traces` work like the omp ones. OpenClaw: the folder `openclaw` plays the home folder (state folders .openclaw and the profile .openclaw-work); after the OpenCode and Antigravity databases, the agent databases of `openclaw.dbOrder` are read with the same dedupe set, each one agent per transcript window (agent id `<database>#<session id>`, relative to this folder); `{"unsupported": true}` marks a database without session tables; `openclaw.discover` lists the databases discovery finds, `openclaw.codexDiscover` the rollouts of the Codex roots next to them (METRICS 2); a trace gives the phase of a window after its row `afterSeq`, after the databases before it; reading must not create any file. Hermes Agent: see `hermes._comment`; its log files are not in `order` (one parser state per log folder) but their modification times are in `mtimes`.

hermes._comment: Hermes Agent (METRICS 4.15). `home` plays the Hermes home; `discover` lists the log files of its log folders. Feed the files of `order` (modification times `mtimes`) to one parser state per log folder, with wall times in `timeZone`, and the shared dedupe set; `sets` gives, per log folder, its malformed API-call lines and one agent per session id (the empty id is the agent of lines without a session tag; agent id = absolute folder path + '#' + id), in the order agents first appear. `traces` give one session's phase after feeding a file up to and including physical line `afterLine`, after the files before it in `order`. `wallTimes` convert a record line's timestamp in a zone (null: not a record line). `homes` resolve the Hermes home from an environment. `rotation` replays a log folder with real renames: `append` writes `lines` (each followed by a newline) or raw `text` to a file and sets its modification time, `rename` and `delete` change files, `read` reads every file of the folder from the offset its identity reached and checks every response key emitted so far and the listed agents. `runtimeConfigs` give config.yaml texts and whether they select the Codex runtime. `codexRuntime` replays a Hermes home (folder `home`, with the profile `p`): `write` sets a file's text (`size`: padded with `#` to that many bytes) and modification time, `remove` deletes it, `append` works like the rotation's, and `read` checks the config.yaml of every log folder, then reads its new lines, and checks each listed log folder's switch, every response key emitted so far and the listed agents.
